e-5438.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis
e-5438.problem:
Given that $\{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j}, \mathbf k\}$ is the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the images of $\mathbf{i},$ $\mathbf{j},$ and $\mathbf{k}$ under the action of a linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ are
$\langle 3, 5, -1 \rangle,$ $\langle 0, 4,3 \rangle,$ and $\langle -1, 5, -2\rangle,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $\mathbf{T}?$
e-5438.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in $\mathbb{R}^3$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $\mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j},$ and $\mathbf k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

e-5436.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
e-5436.problem:
The linear transformation $\mathbf T$ has the standard matrix 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14060116/assets/343c9e46cf59cf4372a563c80dd9010bcece8c04f8babdb95d57c04cdf4a2503.png) 
What are the images of the standard basis vectors $\{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ under the action of $\mathbf T?$
e-5436.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j} \}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot\mathbf{i}$ and $T\cdot\mathbf{j}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 \\ 8 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 \\ 8 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨6,2,0⟩, ⟨−3,5,6⟩, and ⟨−1,2,7⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[6−3−1252067]
b
[−127−356620]
c
[0672526−3−1]
d
[0676−3−1252]
e
[620−356−127]
Submit

decision.explanation: The standard matrix has columns T(i), T(j), and T(k), in that order. Placing the given images as columns yields option a.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Given that ${i,j,k}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨6,2,0⟩,$ $⟨-3,5,6⟩,$ and $⟨-1,2,7⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 1
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨6,2,0⟩, ⟨−3,5,6⟩, and ⟨−1,2,7⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[6−3−1252067]
b
[−127−356620]
c
[0672526−3−1]
d
[0676−3−1252]
e
[620−356−127]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[6−3−1252067].

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis
content.problem: Given that ${i,j,k}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨6,2,0⟩,$ $⟨-3,5,6⟩,$ and $⟨-1,2,7⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 6 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: The columns of the standard matrix are the images of i and j, respectively. Thus the first column is (1,4) and the second is (5,-1), giving option d.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Given that ${i,j}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ and that the images of $i$ and $j$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨1,4⟩$ and $⟨5,-1⟩$, respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 2
?

Given that {i,j} is the standard basis of R2 and that the images of i and j under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨1,4⟩ and ⟨5,−1⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
 [15−41]
b
 [145−1]
c
 [1451]
d
 [154−1]
e
 [−1541]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is T=[154−1].

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms that the images (1,4) and (5,-1) form the first and second columns, giving option d. The submitted option b instead places these images in rows.

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis
content.problem: Given that ${i,j}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ and that the images of $i$ and $j$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨1,4⟩$ and $⟨5,-1⟩$, respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for this linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

before.html:
Question 3
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨3,4,−1⟩, ⟨2,0,7⟩, and ⟨−4,−2,9⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[32−4−24076−1]
b
[−4−2920734−1]
c
[34−1207−4−29]
d
[32−440−2−179]
e
[67940−232−4]
Submit

decision.explanation: The standard matrix has T(i), T(j), and T(k) as its columns, respectively. Using (3,4,-1), (2,0,7), and (-4,-2,9) gives option d.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Given that ${i,j,k}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨3,4,-1⟩,$ $⟨2,0,7⟩,$ and $⟨-4,-2,9⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -4 \\ 4 & 0 & -2 \\ -1 & 7 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

after.html:
Question 3
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨3,4,−1⟩, ⟨2,0,7⟩, and ⟨−4,−2,9⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[32−4−24076−1]
b
[−4−2920734−1]
c
[34−1207−4−29]
d
[32−440−2−179]
e
[67940−232−4]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[32−440−2−179].

content.problem: Given that ${i,j,k}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨3,4,-1⟩,$ $⟨2,0,7⟩,$ and $⟨-4,-2,9⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -4 \\ 4 & 0 & -2 \\ -1 & 7 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 4
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨3,2,−1⟩, ⟨2,−3,1⟩, and ⟨1,−2,3⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
 [3211−232−31]
b
[31213−2213]
c
[321−1132−3−2]
d
[3212−3−2−113]
e
[3212−311−23]
Submit

decision.explanation: Place T(i)=(3,2,-1), T(j)=(2,-3,1), and T(k)=(1,-2,3) as the first, second, and third columns. The resulting standard matrix is option d.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Given that ${i,j,k}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨3,2,-1⟩,$ $⟨2,-3,1⟩,$ and $⟨1,-2,3⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

after.html:
Question 4
?

Given that {i,j,k} is the standard basis of R3 and that the images of i, j, and k under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨3,2,−1⟩, ⟨2,−3,1⟩, and ⟨1,−2,3⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
 [3211−232−31]
b
[31213−2213]
c
[321−1132−3−2]
d
[3212−3−2−113]
e
[3212−311−23]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R3 can be represented as a 3×3 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i,j, and k under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is T=[3212−3−2−113].

verification.explanation: The columns must be (3,2,-1), (2,-3,1), and (1,-2,3), respectively. Option d has exactly these columns and matches the revealed worked solution; the deliberately submitted option a is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Image of the Standard Basis
content.problem: Given that ${i,j,k}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨3,2,-1⟩,$ $⟨2,-3,1⟩,$ and $⟨1,-2,3⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

before.html:
Question 5
?

Given that {i,j} is the standard basis of R2 and that the images of i and j under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨−1,2⟩ and ⟨3,−8⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[−823−1]
b
[−123−8]
c
[3−1−82]
d
[−132−8]
e
[3−12−8]
Submit

decision.explanation: The standard matrix has T(i)=(-1,2) as its first column and T(j)=(3,-8) as its second column, giving option d.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Given that ${i,j}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$ and that the images of $i$ and $j$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨-1,2⟩$ and $⟨3,-8⟩$, respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

after.html:
Question 5
?

Given that {i,j} is the standard basis of R2 and that the images of i and j under the action of a linear transformation T are ⟨−1,2⟩ and ⟨3,−8⟩, respectively, what is the standard matrix of T?

a
[−823−1]
b
[−123−8]
c
[3−1−82]
d
[−132−8]
e
[3−12−8]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is
T=[−132−8].

content.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14060116/assets/09423b097ab02b339f15af831e0e35f59ff88cb00c0ef72d3693ce9f24e6b9dc.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

after.html:
Question 6
?

In the diagram above, i and j are the vectors of the standard basis of R2, while i′ and j′ are their images under the linear transformation T. What is the standard matrix of T?

a
[13−2−3]
b
[−21−33]
c
[1−23−3]
d
[−2−313]
e
[1−2−33]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that i′=[−2−3] and j′=[13].

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

T=[−21−33].

verification.explanation: The diagram and worked solution give T(i)=(-2,-3) and T(j)=(1,3). These form the first and second columns, confirming option b.

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14060116/assets/5aaf29ab4dd2de3d104ca37a71ee66078f985b908465a77ca06ba8ffadd50210.png)

In the diagram above,  $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and  ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14060116/assets/2f0c94bc3100b4fd9754ee822f55e2edbae8475bece3b18ac34f63e6c92267a2.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

In the diagram above, i and j are the vectors of the standard basis of R2, while i′ and j′ are their images under the linear transformation T. What is the standard matrix of T?

EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that i′=[3−3] and j′=[12].

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

T=[31−32].

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

after.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$

Question 9
?

In the diagram above, i and j are the vectors of the standard basis of R2, while i′ and j′ are their images under the linear transformation T. What is the standard matrix of T?

a
[3−112]
b
[−1321]
c
[3−121]
d
[−1231]
e
[31−12]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Every linear transformation in R2 can be represented as a 2×2 matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors i and j under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that i′=[31] and j′=[−12].

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is

T=[3−112].

content.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: The diagram shows T(i)=(1,-1) and T(j)=(-1,-1). These form the first and second columns of the standard matrix, giving option a.

after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14060116/assets/1f22e58fb007553116df6049bbc7cf65c9ce2c84c4846e36258e682be4cc183b.png)

In the diagram above, $i$ and $j$ are the vectors of the standard basis of ${R}^{2}$, while ${i}^{′}$ and ${j}^{′}$ are their images under the linear transformation $T.$
What is the standard matrix of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{2}$ can be represented as a $2\times 2$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of the transformation.

From the diagram, we see that 
${i}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ 
and 
${j}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].

before.html:
Question 11
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[1−4−1−35−20−10]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
[−45−1], [1−30], and [−1−20]
b
[1−4−1], [−35−2], and [0−10]
c
[−310], [5−4−1], and [−2−10]
d
[1−30], [−45−1], and [−1−20]
e
[−35−2], [1−4−1], and [0−10]
Submit

decision.explanation: The images of i, j, and k are the first, second, and third columns of T: (1,-3,0), (-4,5,-1), and (-1,-2,0), respectively. This is option d.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j,k}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j,k}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j,k}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[1−4−1−35−20−10]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
[−45−1], [1−30], and [−1−20]
b
[1−4−1], [−35−2], and [0−10]
c
[−310], [5−4−1], and [−2−10]
d
[1−30], [−45−1], and [−1−20]
e
[−35−2], [1−4−1], and [0−10]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} are the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[100]=[1−30]T(j)=T[010]=[−45−1]T(k)=T[001]=[−1−20]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} by computing the matrix products T⋅i, T⋅j, and T⋅k:

T(i)=T⋅i=[1−4−1−35−20−10][100]=[1−30]T(j)=T⋅j=[1−4−1−35−20−10][010]=[−45−1]T(k)=T⋅k=[1−4−1−35−20−10][001]=[−1−20]

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
content.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j,k}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j,k}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j,k}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 12
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[241−5]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
[4−5] and [21]
b
[1−5] and [24]
c
[21] and [4−5]
d
[12] and [−54]
e
[24] and [1−5]
Submit

decision.explanation: The images of i and j are the first and second columns of T, respectively: (2,1) and (4,-5). This gives option c.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[241−5]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
[4−5] and [21]
b
[1−5] and [24]
c
[21] and [4−5]
d
[12] and [−54]
e
[24] and [1−5]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[21]T(j)=T[01]=[4−5]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

T(i)=T⋅i=[241−5][10]=[21]T(j)=T⋅j=[241−5][01]=[4−5]

verification.explanation: Multiplying T by i=(1,0) selects its first column, (2,1); multiplying by j=(0,1) selects its second column, (4,-5). This confirms option c and agrees with the worked solution.

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
content.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 13
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[231−2]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
 [21] and [3−2]
b
 [3−2] and [21]
c
 [32] and [−21]
d
 [23] and [1−2]
e
 [2−2] and [31]
Submit

decision.explanation: The images of i and j are the first and second columns of T, respectively: (2,1) and (3,-2). This is option a.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[231−2]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
 [21] and [3−2]
b
 [3−2] and [21]
c
 [32] and [−21]
d
 [23] and [1−2]
e
 [2−2] and [31]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[21]T(j)=T[01]=[3−2]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

T(i)=T⋅i=[231−2][10]=[21]T(j)=T⋅j=[231−2][01]=[3−2]

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
content.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[35−1403−1−42]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
[50−4], [34−1], and [−132]
b
[34−1], [−450], and [32−1]
c
[34−1], [50−4], and [−132]
d
[−1−42], [403], and [35−1]
e
[35−1], [403], and [−1−42]
Submit

decision.explanation: The images of i, j, and k are the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively: (3,4,-1), (5,0,-4), and (-1,3,2). This is option c.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j,k}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j,k}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j,k}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[35−1403−1−42]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j,k} of R3 under the action of T?

a
[50−4], [34−1], and [−132]
b
[34−1], [−450], and [32−1]
c
[34−1], [50−4], and [−132]
d
[−1−42], [403], and [35−1]
e
[35−1], [403], and [−1−42]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} are the first, second, and third columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[100]=[34−1]T(j)=T[010]=[50−4]T(k)=T[001]=[−132]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j,k} by computing the matrix products T⋅i, T⋅j, and T⋅k:

T(i)=T⋅i=[35−1403−1−42][100]=[34−1]T(j)=T⋅j=[35−1403−1−42][010]=[50−4]T(k)=T⋅k=[35−1403−1−42][001]=[−132]

verification.explanation: The images of i, j, and k are the first, second, and third columns of T: (3,4,-1), (5,0,-4), and (-1,3,2). Option c matches these images and the revealed worked solution.

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
content.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j,k}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j,k}$ are the first, second, and third columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j,k}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i,$ $T\cdot j,$ and $T\cdot k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ T(k) & =T\cdot k=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 15
?

The linear transformation T has the standard matrix T=[613−2]. What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors {i,j} of R2 under the action of T?

a
[63] and [−12]
b
[61] and [3−2]
c
[−36] and [1−2]
d
[63] and [1−2]
e
[36] and [1−2]
Submit

decision.explanation: The images of i and j are the first and second columns of T, respectively: (6,3) and (1,-2). This is option d.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Method 1

The images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} are the first and second columns of T, respectively.

Therefore, we have the following:

T(i)=T[10]=[63]T(j)=T[01]=[1−2]

Method 2

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis {i,j} by computing the matrix products T⋅i and T⋅j:

T(i)=T⋅i=[613−2][10]=[63]T(j)=T⋅j=[613−2][01]=[1−2]

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Images of the Standard Basis Vectors Under a Given Linear Transformation
content.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
